subject: Re: Trial onboarding — telemetry needs & stress profile
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Patel <anya@fintegrate.ai>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@fintegrate.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Trial onboarding — telemetry needs & stress profile

Hi Anya / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great discussion. Per our call I wanted to capture the immediate next steps on trial setup and ask for a bit more detail on your traffic profile so we can provision the right trial footprint and telemetry hooks. I summarized below and attached a simple CSV you can fill if that’s easier.

Quick summary / asks:
- Success criteria (what will make the trial a win for Fintegrate?): please list 2–3 measurable items (latency thresholds, quality checks, cost targets, failure tolerance).
- Traffic specification: typical RPS, peak burst RPS, median/95th token length, concurrency targets, and any time-of-day seasonality.
- Integration points: will you route traffic through a proxy, or call Redwood API directly from your service? If proxy, which IP ranges should we expect?
- Telemetry: we’ll emit token-level latency and error traces — please confirm which fields you want in the sample events (session_id, user_id, prompt_type, eval_label, etc.).
- Timeline & ownership: propose ideal kickoff date for the trial and primary owners on your side for infra and product.

Proposed Redwood trial plan (high level):
- Day 0–2: infra onboarding + API keys + basic smoke tests
- Day 3–7: ingest sample traffic, enable KV/prefix caching, validate latency 95p
- Week 2: scale to agreed RPS, run 72-hour soak at target concurrency
- Week 3: collect evals, run quality regressions, sign-off on success criteria

Owners on our side: Ben Carter (trial infra / capacity), Marissa Cole (success metrics + evals), me for overall coordination.

Attached: POC-telemetry-template.csv (small template to paste sample X requests), and a sample fintegrate-sample-traffic.yml that shows the expected fields.

Can you send the filled template by end of week? If useful I can carve out 30 min to walk through it.

Best,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0148

From: Anya Patel <anya@fintegrate.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@fintegrate.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial onboarding — telemetry needs & stress profile

Thanks Irene — appreciate the clear next steps. I filled the attached CSV and included some additional notes below. Attaching our filled POC-telemetry-template.csv and a short sample of production traces.

Fintegrate trial success criteria (initial):
1) Median end-to-end latency (prompt in -> first token out) < 220ms at baseline RPS (200 RPS)
2) 95th percentile latency < 900ms during 10-minute bursts up to 600 RPS
3) Response quality: BLEU-style match on our labelled prompts >= 0.78 for top-3 generation checks

Traffic profile (current prod footprint, week-day average):
- Typical sustained RPS: 180–220 RPS (most regions aggregate)
- Planned trial target sustained RPS: 200 RPS
- Burst profile: brief bursts up to 600 RPS (10–15 seconds) 3–4x per hour during business hours
- Median token lengths: prompt 120 tokens, response 220 tokens; 95th token length ~ 1,100 tokens (long-form docs)
- Concurrent sessions: ~45 concurrent long-lived sessions (websocket style), up to 250 concurrent short calls
- Time windows: heavy between 08:00–18:00 PT, lighter at night

Integration: for the trial we will call Redwood API directly from our inference service; no proxy. We’ll provide a CIDR range for our egress shortly.

Owners:
- Product owner: Anya Patel (me)
- Infra lead: Tom Liu (cc) — he’ll own traffic generation and secrets

Questions from our side:
- Can Redwood support 95p latency tracking broken down by token position (first/25%/median/last)?
- During bursts, do you recommend bumping up kv-cache or batching limits?

Tom and I can do a quick sync tomorrow at 09:30 PT if that works.

Best,
Anya Patel
Head of Product — Fintegrate
anya@fintegrate.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Patel <anya@fintegrate.ai>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@fintegrate.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial onboarding — telemetry needs & stress profile

Hi Anya / Tom —

Thanks for the detailed numbers — that helps a lot. Quick answers and a proposed config for the trial based on your profile:

1) Observability: we can emit 1p/25p/50p/75p/95p/99p per-token-position buckets and also histogram exports for first-token latency. We’ll include token_position labels (first/quarter/mid/last) in traces.

2) Trial configuration (proposal):
- Baseline nodes: 2 dedicated GPU workers sized for medium-seq (up to 1k tokens)
- Autoscale policy: scale to 6 workers for sustained >300 RPS, with 30 sec scale windows for bursts
- KV cache: enabled with prefix caching; recommend enabling reply-level caching for repeated prompt templates
- Batching: dynamic batching with 25ms max wait; for burst windows we’ll temporarily relax to 40ms to increase throughput if latency targets are still met

3) Soak & stress plan:
- Day 1–2: onboarding + smoke tests at 50 RPS
- Day 3: ramp to 200 RPS baseline, validate median latency
- Day 4: run 72-hr soak at 200 RPS with scheduled 10–15s bursts to 600 RPS (every 15–30 mins during business hours)
- Day 7: final quality run and success criteria review

4) Owners + next steps:
- Ben Carter: capacity & soak orchestration (I’ll provision infra and run the burst tests)
- Marissa Cole: evaluation harness and quality checks (she’ll own metric dashboards + BLEU collections)
- Irene Choi: contract/credits and overall coordination

Ben: can you provision the trial environment tomorrow and share the test endpoints?
Marissa: I’ll drop the eval harness template link in the shared Drive.

Thanks — we’ll be ready to run the ramp on Thu (2026-09-16) if you confirm the CIDR and initial API call samples.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@fintegrate.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial onboarding — telemetry needs & stress profile

Thanks team — confirmed schedule and a couple small clarifications.

- We can confirm API samples and CIDR today; will send to Ben by EOD.
- For the 72-hr soak, can you include per-worker CPU/GPU utilization traces in the telemetry exports? That will help our infra team correlate throttling events.
- One small change to the burst cadence: rather than every 15–30 mins, we’ll do 4x per hour with two of the bursts being back-to-back (to mimic short spiky user behavior).

We’re happy with Thu kickoff (2026-09-16) and will aim to have filled CSV + sample traces to you by tonight.

Tom Liu
Infra Lead — Fintegrate
Tom.Liu@fintegrate.ai
